requirement_text:
Functional Requirements

Torrent Search

REQ-1: Torrent search will share the same search bar with the streaming search. REQ-2: Database of torrent sites can be updated via the internet.
REQ-3: There will be a tick box to allow the user to choose to include torrent searching in the search.

REQ-4: Query will retrieve the no. of seed and peers, size of the file, date posted and a link to the webpage itself.

REQ-5: If no results are found on a search it will display a message “No results were found for this search.”

REQ-6: Results will be arranged in size/date/alphabetical order by clicking on the column headers.

REQ-7: There will be page button for the user to navigate the results.

Video Stream Search

REQ-1: Streaming search will share the same search bar with the torrent search. REQ-2: Database of video hosting and video linking sites can be updated via the
internet.

REQ-3: There will be a tick box to allow the user to choose to include video host searching in the search.
 
REQ-4: There will be a tick box to allow the user to choose to include video link searching in the search.

REQ-5: Query to video hosting sites will retrieve full video name, length, date posted and a link to the video itself.

REQ-6: Query to video link sites will retrieve the show’s name, episode name and a link to the webpage itself.

REQ-7: If no results are found on a search it will display a message “No results were found for this search.”

REQ-8: Results will be arranged in length/date/alphabetical order by clicking on the column headers.

REQ-9: There will be page button for the user to navigate the results.


Use case Scenarios

3.1 Torrent Search

3.1.1 Description and Priority


The user will give a search-term that will search through a database of compatible torrent websites that are added by the development team. The results of this search will be displayed as web links in a tab on the program’s main window. This is one of the main features of the software and therefore has a high priority for development.


3.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences


User ticks torrent tick box – system will now query the torrent websites in its database when a search is started.

User enters search term and starts search – system sends queries to the torrent websites in its database based on the search term. Results for this query will then be sent to the torrent tab in the program where they will display information such as website, seeds, peers, size, date posted and a link for the webpage.

User sorts the search results by clicking once on a column header – system sorts all results by descending/ascending order.

User clicks on next page button – system displays the next set of results for the search.

3.2 Video Stream Search


3.2.1 Description and Priority


This feature will search a term the user enters, through a database of compatible video streaming websites that are added by the development team. The video websites will range from sites that actually host video such as MegaVideo, YouTube, etc as well as websites that show links to videos hosted on other sites such as surfthechannel.com, alluc.org, etc. The results will be displayed in a tab on the programs main window. This tab will be split horizontally into two sections, the
top half for the video hosting sites and the bottom half for the video link sites. This is another of the main features of the software and also has a higher priority for
development.


3.2.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences


User ticks streaming host tick box – system will now query the video hosting sites in its database when a search is started. Hosting sites will include the actual videos on their servers, e.g. YouTube.

User ticks streaming links tick box – system will now query the video link sites in its database when a search is started. The link sites will include external video links to different video hosting sites, e.g. surfthechannel.com.

User enters search term and starts search – system sends queries to the video websites in its database based on the search term. Results for this query will then be sent to the video stream tab in the program. The hosting half of the tab displays the website, full video name, length and date posted. The link half of the tab displays the website and video name (e.g. combination of the show’s name and the episode name).

User sorts the search results by clicking once on the column header – system sorts all results by descending/ascending order.

User filters websites they want to be shown in the results – system removes unselected websites from the results.

User clicks on next page button – system displays the next set of results for the search.

plan.objective: Integrated search flow for torrent and streaming results with shared search bar, selectable sources, querying, display, sorting, filtering, pagination, and no-results handling.
decision_strategy: Use one decision to select the enabled search path(s) from the shared search bar.
Use explicit no-results branches for torrent and streaming searches, then continue to result interactions where applicable.
concurrency_strategy: Model streaming host and streaming link querying as concurrent branches with a fork and join.
exception_strategy: No terminating exception flow is specified beyond displaying the no-results message, so no separate exception handler node is used.
termination_strategy: Terminate after the torrent pagination/display path and after the streaming pagination/display path.
Every path from the shared search bar converges into a final node.

diagram.title: Integrated search flow for torrent and streaming results with shared search bar, selectable sources, querying, display, sorting, filtering, pagination, and no-results handling.

validation.summary: 0 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 1.000. Coverage score: 1.000. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 1.000.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most required search, query, display, sorting, filtering, pagination, and no-results behaviors, but it has one important semantic gap: the streaming search requirement explicitly calls for separate handling of video hosting and video link retrieval/display, while the diagram models them as parallel queries without clearly preserving the required split outputs in a way that distinguishes the two result types through the search flow. Also, the torrent search no-results branch appears to flow into sorting/pagination without showing a distinct termination or explicit return to the results flow after the message, which is acceptable if interpreted as continuation, but the diagram is ambiguous. Overall, the diagram is largely compliant with minor semantic ambiguity.

defects.description: The streaming search flow does not clearly preserve the required distinction between video hosting results and video link results as separate outputs after querying. The requirements specify that hosting sites must retrieve and display full video name, length, date posted, and link, while link sites must retrieve and display show name and episode name; the diagram merges both branches through a generic send/display sequence and a shared no-results/sort/filter/pagination flow, which obscures the distinct result handling required by the specification.
defects.evidence: The requirements separate streaming behavior into two distinct retrieval/display contracts: R12 requires hosting sites to retrieve full video name, length, date posted, and a link; R13 requires link sites to retrieve show name, episode name, and a link. In the diagram, N19 forks to N20 and N21, but both merge at N22 and then proceed through a generic N23 'Send streaming results' and N26 'Streaming results found?' decision, followed by shared sort/filter/pagination actions. The individual display actions N24 and N25 occur, but the later control flow no longer distinguishes the two output types in a way that preserves their separate required semantics.
defects.suggested_action: Refactor the streaming branch so that hosting and link results remain explicitly separated through their respective display paths, with any shared operations applied only after the diagram has clearly represented the two required result structures. Ensure the flow makes it unambiguous which data fields are produced and shown by each source type.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most required torrent and streaming search behaviors, including shared search bar, database updates, searching, results display, no-results handling, sorting, pagination, and streaming source selection. However, two user tick-box requirements remain directly unrepresented as distinct actions, and there is a semantic issue in the streaming branch where source-specific query behavior is collapsed into an unspecific combined flow, obscuring the required separate host/link query conditions.

defects.description: Requirement R25 is still not represented as a distinct diagram element: the user tick box for selecting streaming host search is not explicitly modeled as its own action.
defects.evidence: R25 requires: "The user ticks the streaming host tick box." The diagram only routes from the search-type decision to a combined streaming-query fork and includes a guard "hosting selected" on E21, but no separate node/action explicitly represents the user ticking the hosting tick box.
defects.suggested_action: Add an explicit user action node for ticking the streaming host tick box and connect it to the streaming selection flow before the query fork.

defects.description: Requirement R27 is still not represented as a distinct diagram element: the user tick box for selecting streaming link search is not explicitly modeled as its own action.
defects.evidence: R27 requires: "The user ticks the streaming links tick box." The diagram only routes from the search-type decision to a combined streaming-query fork and includes a guard "link selected" on E22, but no separate node/action explicitly represents the user ticking the links tick box.
defects.suggested_action: Add an explicit user action node for ticking the streaming links tick box and connect it to the streaming selection flow before the query fork.

defects.description: The streaming query behavior is modeled as a combined fork, but the required conditional query actions for hosting and link sites are not explicitly separated from the selection steps, making the dependence on R25/R27 less clear in the activity semantics.
defects.evidence: R26 and R28 each require that when a search is started, the system queries the respective site type based on the corresponding tick box selection. The current diagram uses N19 "Query streaming sources" as a fork to both N20 and N21, with guards "hosting selected" and "link selected," but the actual user selection actions (R25, R27) are not separately modeled and the fork is triggered directly after the shared search-term entry flow.
defects.suggested_action: Model the host and link selections as explicit user actions and route the query actions from those selections so the conditions for R26 and R28 are unambiguous.

diagram.title: Integrated search flow for torrent and streaming results with shared search bar, selectable sources, querying, display, sorting, filtering, pagination, and no-results handling.

validation.summary: 0 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 1.000. Coverage score: 1.000. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 1.000.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most required search, query, display, sorting, filtering, pagination, and no-results behaviors, but it has one important semantic gap: the streaming search requirement explicitly calls for separate handling of video hosting and video link retrieval/display, while the diagram models them as parallel queries without clearly preserving the required split outputs in a way that distinguishes the two result types through the search flow. Also, the torrent search no-results branch appears to flow into sorting/pagination without showing a distinct termination or explicit return to the results flow after the message, which is acceptable if interpreted as continuation, but the diagram is ambiguous. Overall, the diagram is largely compliant with minor semantic ambiguity.

defects.description: The streaming search flow does not clearly preserve the required distinction between video hosting results and video link results as separate outputs after querying. The requirements specify that hosting sites must retrieve and display full video name, length, date posted, and link, while link sites must retrieve and display show name and episode name; the diagram merges both branches through a generic send/display sequence and a shared no-results/sort/filter/pagination flow, which obscures the distinct result handling required by the specification.
defects.evidence: The requirements separate streaming behavior into two distinct retrieval/display contracts: R12 requires hosting sites to retrieve full video name, length, date posted, and a link; R13 requires link sites to retrieve show name, episode name, and a link. In the diagram, N19 forks to N20 and N21, but both merge at N22 and then proceed through a generic N23 'Send streaming results' and N26 'Streaming results found?' decision, followed by shared sort/filter/pagination actions. The individual display actions N24 and N25 occur, but the later control flow no longer distinguishes the two output types in a way that preserves their separate required semantics.
defects.suggested_action: Refactor the streaming branch so that hosting and link results remain explicitly separated through their respective display paths, with any shared operations applied only after the diagram has clearly represented the two required result structures. Ensure the flow makes it unambiguous which data fields are produced and shown by each source type.
